page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 with VNNI extensions, AES encryption support, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance runs on the KVM hypervisor and does not include bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage along with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations show average multi-core compute capability alongside lower single-thread throughput. In multi-threaded execution, the instance produced a stress-ng score of 6986.33, a PassMark CPU score of 8224.85, and achieved 6.6 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 49.44 GB/sec for large block reads and 36.78 GB/sec for large block writes. Single-core evaluations reveal lower per-thread throughput, with Geekbench single-core registering at 1140.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1312.09, both landing in the lower benchmark tiers.

From an infrastructure perspective, ecs.c6.2xlarge balances dedicated CPU allocation against a lean memory profile, avoiding the higher overhead associated with memory-dense configurations. Because the server lacks local NVMe disks and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network limit, I/O-intensive database and static serving workloads may experience bottlenecks. The instance is suited for compute-focused tasks that scale horizontally across cores, such as software compilation pipelines, batch processing jobs, background task workers, and microservices.
